newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday thanks to a technical rebound on the domestic A share market and one new A share issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rose sharply to 6.50 percent from 3.00 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 10.7 million losts from 5.6 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the rebound on the A share markets on Monday boosted sentiment on the repo market and supported the rates.
"Some institutions borrowed heavily on the repo market, pushing up the rates," one trader said.
Traders said the Shenzhen A share issue was particularly responsible for rises in the early-maturing repo contracts.
Traders said they believed the rates would continue on an upward trend this week due a number of new A shares issues.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed in slow trading on Monday with the reviving A share markets absorbing funds from the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 120.94 yuan from 120.82 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell sharply to 827,366 lots from 1.1 million lots.

Traders said a large number of new A share issues this week were likely to depress sentiment on the spot market but that the high yields of the existing contracts would prevent them from falling sharply.
They said they believed the prices would move around the current levels in the next few days.
